proofs.proof_tex:
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ipw\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) gives the stronger uniform first-moment statement
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}}
 E_P\!\left[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)\right]
 \le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
\]
The radius is strictly positive because \(B>0\), \(q>0\), \(\lambda_{nm}>0\), and \(n,m\ge2\).  Therefore Markov's inequality gives, for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}}
 P\!\left\{\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)>
 t a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\right\}\le \frac Ct.
\]
This is the asserted uniform \(O_P(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) bound.  The construction of \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and the proof of the moment bound use only the score matrix and contain no loading family, so no factor depending on \(|\mathcal G_n|\) occurs.

For the final assertion, Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:adaptive\mbox{-}endogenous\mbox{-}target\mbox{-}obstruction}\) supplies a sequence \(P_n\) in the same class and constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) such that \(b_{nn}\to0\) and
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_n\!\left\{
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)>c_0\right\}\ge c_1.
\]
If the IPW--SVD loss were uniformly \(O_P(b_{nm})\), then for \(\varepsilon=c_1/2\) some fixed \(T<\infty\) would make the displayed probability at threshold \(Tb_{nn}\) at most \(\varepsilon\) eventually.  Since \(Tb_{nn}<c_0\) eventually, this contradicts the preceding lower probability.  The witness evaluates \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\) and hence proves no impossibility statement for a different estimator.

For \(Q_1,Q_2\in\mathbb O_{n,r}\), set
\[
 \delta(Q_1,Q_2)=\min_{R\in\mathbb O_r}
 \lVert Q_1R-Q_2\rVert_{2,\infty}.
\]
The minimum exists because \(\mathbb O_r\) is compact.  Right multiplication by an orthogonal matrix preserves every row Euclidean norm.  Consequently \(\delta\) is symmetric.  If \(R_{12}\) and \(R_{23}\) are minimizers for \((Q_1,Q_2)\) and \((Q_2,Q_3)\), respectively, then
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \delta(Q_1,Q_3)
 &\le\lVert Q_1R_{12}R_{23}-Q_3\rVert_{2,\infty}\\
 &\le\lVert(Q_1R_{12}-Q_2)R_{23}\rVert_{2,\infty}
 +\lVert Q_2R_{23}-Q_3\rVert_{2,\infty}\\
 &=\delta(Q_1,Q_2)+\delta(Q_2,Q_3).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Multiplication by the positive constant \(\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\) proves the triangle and reverse-triangle inequalities for \(\mathcal L\).

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:blind\mbox{-}ratio\mbox{-}expansion}\), under exactly the hypotheses in the statement, gives
\[
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U^{\mathrm B})=O_P(d_{nm}).
\]
Let \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) denote the radius in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:ipw\mbox{-}rowwise\mbox{-}upper}\).  Since \(q<1/2\),
\(q^{-1/2}\le q^{-1}\).  Bounded aspect ratio also gives a constant \(C\), depending only on \(c_-\) and \(c_+\), for which
\(\log(e(n+m))\le C\log(en)\).  Hence the expression inside the truncation defining \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) is at most a constant times the one defining \(d_{nm}\).  Because
\(1\wedge(Cx)\le(1\vee C)(1\wedge x)\) for \(x\ge0\),
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}=O(d_{nm}).
\]
The recorded-IPW theorem therefore implies
\[
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)=O_P(d_{nm}).
\]

By the reverse-triangle inequality and the definitions of \(\rho_{nm}\) and \(\widehat\rho_{nm}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U)-\rho_{nm}\right|
 &\le\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U^{\mathrm B}),\\
 |\widehat\rho_{nm}-\rho_{nm}|
 &=\left|\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},\widehat U^{\mathrm I})
 -\mathcal L(U^{\mathrm B},U)\right|\\
 &\le\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U^{\mathrm B})
 +\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Substitution of the two stochastic bounds proves both conclusions.  No comparison between \(d_{nm}\) and \(b_{nm}\) is used.

added_lemmas.statement:
Put
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}=
 \sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\left[1\wedge
 \frac B{\lambda_{nm}}\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}+
 \frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}\right].
\]
There is a universal constant \(C<\infty\) such that, for every \(n,m\ge2\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P\!\left[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)\right]
 \le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
\]
Thus the loose IPW--SVD upper bound holds in the same expected normalized maximum-row loss used by the minimax lower benchmark.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a law \(P\) in the predictable class and expose cells in the row-major order of \(\mathrm{def:global\mbox{-}filtration}\).  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:ipw\mbox{-}identification}\), each \(E_{ij}\) has conditional mean zero given \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).  Sequential randomization and bounded outcomes give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P\!\left[(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij})^2
 \mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\right]
 &=E_P\!\left[
 \frac{Y_{ij}(1)^2}{p_{ij}}+
 \frac{Y_{ij}(0)^2}{1-p_{ij}}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\right]\\
 &\le \frac{2B^2}{q}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The equality follows by first conditioning on the two potential outcomes and using sequential randomization; both divisions are valid by overlap.  Since \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\), conditional variance is no larger than the displayed conditional second moment.  Moreover \(|Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}|\le B/q\), \(|M_{ij}|\le2B\), and \(q<1/2\), whence
\[
 |E_{ij}|\le \frac{2B}{q}.
\]

Introduce the self-adjoint dilation
\[
 \Delta_{ij}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 0&E_{ij}e_ie_j^\top\\
 E_{ij}e_je_i^\top&0
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its norm is \(|E_{ij}|\), and its square has diagonal blocks
\(E_{ij}^2e_ie_i^\top\) and \(E_{ij}^2e_je_j^\top\).  Therefore the predictable quadratic variation of the sum of the dilations obeys
\[
 \left\lVert\sum_{i,j}E_P[\Delta_{ij}^2
 \mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\right\rVert
 \le v_{nm}:=\frac{2B^2(n\vee m)}q.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:tropp\mbox{-}matrix\mbox{-}freedman}\), applied to both signs of this \((n+m)\)-dimensional martingale, consequently gives
\[
 P\{\lVert E\rVert\ge t\}
 \le2(n+m)\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2/2}{v_{nm}+R_{nm}t/3}\right\},
 \qquad R_{nm}=\frac{2B}{q}.
\]
Indeed, the terminal dilation has operator norm \(\lVert E\rVert\).  Solving the quadratic inequality in this tail bound shows that, with \(L_{nm}=\log(2(n+m))\), for every \(x\ge0\),
\[
 P\!\left\{\lVert E\rVert>
 \sqrt{2v_{nm}(L_{nm}+x)}+
 \frac{2R_{nm}}3(L_{nm}+x)\right\}\le e^{-x}.
\]
Integration of this bound is legitimate because the increments are bounded.  Using
\(\sqrt{L_{nm}+x}\le\sqrt{L_{nm}}+\sqrt x\),
\(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\,dx=1\), and
\(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\sqrt x\,dx<\infty\), yields
\[
 E_P\lVert E\rVert
 \le C B\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}+
 \frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}
 =:C\eta_{nm}.
\]
Every bound so far is uniform in \(P\).

It remains to pass from operator error to the declared loss without imposing predictability on the singular factors.  Let \(P_U=UU^\top\), and let \((\widehat U,\widehat\Sigma,\widehat V)\) be the leading rank-\(r\) singular triple of \(M+E\).  Exact rank gives \((I-P_U)M=0\), while the signal floor and the singular-value min--max formula imply, on \(\{\lVert E\rVert\le\lambda_{nm}/2\}\),
\[
 \sigma_r(\widehat\Sigma)
 \ge\sigma_r(M)-\lVert E\rVert
 \ge\lambda_{nm}-\lVert E\rVert>0.
\]
Projecting \((M+E)\widehat V=\widehat U\widehat\Sigma\) onto the orthogonal complement of \(U\) therefore gives
\[
 \lVert(I-P_U)\widehat U\rVert
 \le\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}-\lVert E\rVert}
 \le\frac{2\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}.
\]
Diagonalizing the principal-angle cosines of \(U^\top\widehat U\) and using
\(2(1-\cos t)\le2\sin^2t\) supplies an \(R\in\mathbb O_r\) such that
\[
 \lVert\widehat UR-U\rVert
 \le\sqrt2\lVert(I-P_U)\widehat U\rVert.
\]
Off the event \(\{\lVert E\rVert\le\lambda_{nm}/2\}\), the left side is at most two.  Since \(\lVert Q\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\lVert Q\rVert\), both cases combine to give the deterministic inequality
\[
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)
 \le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(1\wedge\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}\right).
\]
The fixed tie rule ensures that the leading left singular vectors of \(\mathcal P_r(M+E)\) are the chosen leading left singular vectors of \(M+E\).  Finally, concavity of \(x\mapsto1\wedge x\), Jensen's inequality, and the expectation bound above yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)
 &\le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 E_P\left[1\wedge\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}\right]\\
 &\le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(1\wedge\frac{\eta_{nm}}{\lambda_{nm}}\right)
 \le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Taking the supremum over the declared class proves the result.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(r\), \(K\), and \(\mu>1\).  There are constants \(c_0,c_1,c,C>0\), depending only on these fixed quantities, \(q\), and the aspect bounds, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n,m\), whenever \(b_{nm}\le c_0\) and \(\lambda_{nm}\le c_1B\sqrt{nm}\),
\[
 c b_{nm}\le
 \inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)]
 \le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm},
\]
where
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}=
 \sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\left[1\wedge
 \frac B{\lambda_{nm}}\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}+
 \frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}\right].
\]
The two endpoints use the same expected normalized maximum-row loss.  The bounds need not match: the endogenous-target obstruction rules out \(b_{nm}\)-attainment by recorded IPW--SVD, but does not rule it out for every estimator in \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex: The first inequality is exactly Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:adaptive\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}lower}\), whose lower-bound laws form a constant-propensity subclass of the same predictable class.  By \(\mathrm{def:observed\mbox{-}estimators}\), every member of \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal O_{n,m}=\sigma(A,Y,p)\).  The recorded score is a measurable function of \((A,Y,p)\), and the deterministic rank projection and fixed tie rule are measurable; hence \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).  Evaluating the infimum at this admissible estimator proves the middle inequality.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ipw\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) proves the last inequality under the same class, loss, and sampling law.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:adaptive\mbox{-}endogenous\mbox{-}target\mbox{-}obstruction}\) concerns only the risk of \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\), so it cannot strengthen the first inequality to a lower bound above order \(b_{nm}\) for all estimators.  This proves the bracket and its stated scope.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(n\to\infty\), \(c_-\le m/n\le c_+\), and \(r,\mu,K,q\) are fixed, and define
\[
 d_{nm}=\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\left[1\wedge
 \frac B{\lambda_{nm}}\left\{
 q^{-1}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}+q^{-3}\log(en)
 \right\}\right].
\]
If \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), then the truncations in both \(b_{nm}\) and \(d_{nm}\) are eventually inactive and
\[
 b_{nm}\asymp\frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}},
 \qquad
 d_{nm}\asymp\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\,b_{nm}.
\]
In particular \(d_{nm}/b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt n\to\infty\), so \(d_{nm}=O(b_{nm})\) is not a nonempty fixed-complexity subregime under \(b_{nm}=o(1)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By the geometric-rate definition and bounded aspect ratio,
\[
 \sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\asymp n^{-1/2}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \sqrt{nm}\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\asymp\sqrt n.
\]
Because \(r,\mu,K,q\) are fixed positive constants, the untruncated expression in the lower/reference-scale definition is therefore
\[
 \frac{B\sqrt{nm}}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\log(en)}\,b^0_{nm}
 \asymp\frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}.
\]
The hypothesis \(b_{nm}=o(1)\) makes this expression smaller than one eventually, proving the first equivalence and showing that the truncation defining \(b_{nm}\) is inactive.

Set
\[
 x_{nm}=\frac B{\lambda_{nm}}
 \left\{q^{-1}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}
 +q^{-3}\log(en)\right\}.
\]
Bounded aspect ratio gives
\[
 \sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}\asymp\sqrt{n\log(en)},
\]
whereas
\[
 \frac{\log(en)}{\sqrt{n\log(en)}}
 =\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
With fixed \(q\), it follows that
\[
 x_{nm}\asymp\frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}asymp b_{nm}=o(1).
\]
Thus the truncation in \(d_{nm}\) is also eventually inactive, and its definition gives
\[
 d_{nm}=\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\,x_{nm}
 \asymp\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\,b_{nm}.
\]
Since \(r\) and \(\mu\) are fixed and \(n\to\infty\), division by the positive \(b_{nm}\) proves the divergence and the final assertion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)\), define
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}=
 \sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\left[1\wedge
 \frac B{\lambda_{nm}}\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}+
 \frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}\right].
\]
Then recorded-propensity IPW--SVD satisfies
\(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)=O_P(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\).  This maximum-row assertion is pointwise in the target and contains no factor depending on \(|\mathcal G_n|\).  In general the displayed IPW--SVD conclusion cannot replace \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) by the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\), as witnessed by Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:adaptive\mbox{-}endogenous\mbox{-}target\mbox{-}obstruction}\).  That witness concerns this estimator only and does not assert that every observed-data estimator has risk larger than order \(b_{nm}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing final sentence can be read as an estimator-independent minimax obstruction.  The accepted witness evaluates only recorded IPW--SVD, so the proposed claim explicitly restricts the nonattainment conclusion to that estimator while retaining the proved upper rate.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Uniformly over sequences \(P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)\) that satisfy propensity-path stability, the primitive oracle blind gap, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), define
\[
 d_{nm}=\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\left[1\wedge
 \frac B{\lambda_{nm}}\left\{
 q^{-1}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}+q^{-3}\log(en)
 \right\}\right].
\]
Then
\[
 \left|\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm B},U)-\rho_{nm}\right|=O_P(d_{nm}),
 \qquad
 |\widehat\rho_{nm}-\rho_{nm}|=O_P(d_{nm}).
\]
Thus the observed blind-versus-recorded discrepancy is certified at the explicit \(d_{nm}\) resolution; no \(b_{nm}\)-scale equivalence is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Under bounded aspect ratio with fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), the declared radii satisfy \(d_{nm}/b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt n\to\infty\).  Thus the old conditional \(b_{nm}\)-scale iff has no fixed-complexity asymptotic regime; the honest theorem consists of the two unconditional \(d_{nm}\)-resolution inequalities.

prose_updates.tldr: Recorded propensities identify the causal effect matrix and make the entrywise IPW errors a bounded row-major martingale difference array.  On the frozen predictable class the strongest common-risk statement is the honest bracket \(c b_{nm}\le\inf_{\widetilde U}\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\le\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)]\le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\).  Thus \(b_{nm}\) is a minimax lower/reference scale, not a matched frontier.  The endogenous-target construction rules out uniform \(b_{nm}\)-attainment by recorded IPW--SVD only; whether another observed-data estimator closes the bracket remains open.  Blind row scaling is certified only at the explicit \(d_{nm}\) resolution: both its causal loss and its observed disagreement differ from total drift by \(O_P(d_{nm})\).  With fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\), bounded aspect ratio, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), one has \(d_{nm}/b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt n\), so no \(b_{nm}\)-scale iff is claimed.  The rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law remains an explicit failure witness for blind scaling and a HeartSteps II stress design.  For predeclared dense families, direct finite-sample bands have a separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) multiplicity cost and make no feasible-multiplier exactness claim.

project_justification.gap: Published independent-mask rowwise matrix results do not settle causal effect-subspace risk under history-predictable assignment.  On the present effect-only low-rank class, a constant-propensity packing yields the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\), while a matrix-Freedman and deterministic subspace argument yields only \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) for recorded IPW--SVD.  The accepted endogenous-target example prevents labeling the latter estimator as \(b_{nm}\)-optimal, but it does not prove an estimator-independent lower bound above \(b_{nm}\).
project_justification.niche: The contribution is an explicit same-loss minimax bracket for a causal row subspace under predictable masks, together with an estimator-specific obstruction, a calibrated blind-normalization resolution theorem, and conservative simultaneous causal-contrast bands whose entropy cost is kept separate from the subspace scales.
project_justification.fill: The project proves an expected normalized maximum-row upper bound for recorded IPW--SVD, combines it with the constant-propensity minimax lower bound in one risk criterion, and records the remaining rate gap.  It proves two unconditional \(d_{nm}\)-resolution inequalities for blind scaling and shows algebraically that the former \(d_{nm}=O(b_{nm})\) premise is unavailable in the fixed-complexity \(b_{nm}=o(1)\) regime.  It also supplies the explicit Markov witness and a direct finite-sample union-bound band with separate family-size inflation.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW--SVD uses the known predictable propensities and requires no estimated treatment nuisance.  Its expected-risk guarantee follows from bounded matrix-martingale concentration and a deterministic singular-subspace bound.  The blind procedure replaces entrywise propensities by a clipped empirical row fraction; propensity-path stability and the primitive oracle gap control its tangent expansion only at the explicit \(d_{nm}\) resolution.  The observed discrepancy compares blind and recorded fits at that same resolution and is not advertised as a \(b_{nm}\)-scale certificate.  Simultaneous bands use the direct recorded-IPW contrast and deterministic variance envelopes; leave-one-cell-out residuals and multiplier studentization are not needed for the conservative coverage theorem.

prose_updates.related_work:
Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis are the closest rowwise estimator comparator: their public Algorithm 1, Theorem 3.2, and Corollary 3.3 analyze separate empirical-row-scaled SVD fits for two low-rank arm means under independent Bernoulli assignment.  Their geometric rowwise matrix-error scale motivates \(b^0_{nm}\), but their theorem does not cover history-predictable masks, effect-only low rank, the effect matrix's left singular space, or the present minimax criterion.  Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen prove two-to-infinity upper and lower bounds for an independently sampled low-rank matrix with independent noise; those results inform the deterministic perturbation and local packing architecture but do not make the causal target predictable under the row-major filtration.  The present result is therefore an honest bracket rather than a claimed matched extension of either paper.

Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey support the recorded-propensity martingale-score reduction, and Tropp supplies the bounded-increment matrix Freedman inequality used for the upper moment bound.  Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah study adaptive nearest-neighbor estimation of unit-by-time arm means under an exogenous factor model, a different target and structural class.  Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi; Sun, Zhu, and Dubin; Bai and Ng; Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen; Choi and Yuan; Mao, Wong, and Chen; and Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan address outcome completion, treatment effects on treated cells, entrywise or Frobenius loss, or fixed missingness structures.  None supplies the missing estimator-independent upper rate for the present predictable effect-subspace class, and the current effect-only rank condition does not imply their outcome-matrix assumptions.

Khan and Ugander analyze scalar affine normalization under independent indicators; the blind row-fraction SVD and its \(0.25/0.75\) Markov witness are new objects here and do not refute that published procedure.  Belloni and Oliveira and Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu motivate high-dimensional martingale or multiplier inference, but the retained simultaneous theorem uses direct finite-sample Freedman radii and a union bound only.  Its \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) factor is a query-family entropy cost, not part of either subspace scale.  Spruijt-Metz et al. make saved propensities and omission sensitivity operationally relevant for the HeartSteps II consumer.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Operator-norm martingale concentration followed by a deterministic subspace inequality pays the factor \(\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\), producing \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\).  The frozen class permits the target singular factors to depend on earlier outcomes, so the usual leave-one-row argument cannot simply treat those factors as predictable; the explicit obstruction shows that this is substantive for IPW--SVD.  The minimax lower scale \(b_{nm}\) therefore remains separated from the available upper rate.  For blind normalization, the ratio residual and stochastic spectral perturbation give resolution \(d_{nm}\); at fixed complexity and bounded aspect ratio, \(d_{nm}/b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt n\) whenever \(b_{nm}=o(1)\).  The separate arm means in the denominator derivative are not estimable at a claimed frontier rate under the current effect-only low-rank assumptions.  No residual covariance consistency, positive random studentizer, or feasible multiplier exactness is assumed or claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Identification is given by the recorded IPW conditional mean.  The proved statistical statement is the expected-risk bracket between the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\) and the loose IPW--SVD radius \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\); these rates are not claimed to match.  The adaptive endogenous-target construction refutes only uniform \(b_{nm}\)-attainment by the specified IPW--SVD estimator.  It does not show that every estimator measurable from \(A,Y,p\) fails at that scale, so minimax tightness and the sharp constant remain open.  The blind procedure is introduced here and is certified only up to \(d_{nm}\); no unconditional \(b_{nm}\)-scale validity criterion or feasible tangent correction is claimed.  The \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is a boundary example for that procedure, not a refutation of a published method.  Simultaneous inference is supplied by conservative finite-sample direct-IPW radii, not by asymptotic exactness of the frozen leave-one-cell-out multiplier statistic.

statement_notes.justification: This is the explicit achievable side for the specified recorded-propensity IPW--SVD estimator; the companion moment proposition places it in the expected-loss criterion used by the converse.
statement_notes.gap: The rate is \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\), not the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\).  The endogenous-target witness rules out replacing it by \(b_{nm}\) for this estimator but says nothing conclusive about all observed-data estimators.
statement_notes.consumer: Designers obtain a conservative, fully explicit row-subspace error radius under recorded predictable randomization.

statement_notes.justification: This proposition is the headline same-risk synthesis: the converse and achievability sides are both stated in expected normalized maximum-row loss.
statement_notes.gap: The endpoints \(b_{nm}\) and \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) need not coincide; closing this minimax gap is the residual question.
statement_notes.consumer: Trial designers can separate an information-theoretic lower benchmark from the guarantee of the concrete IPW--SVD fit.

statement_notes.justification: The constant-propensity packing establishes \(b_{nm}\) as a legal minimax lower/reference scale inside the frozen predictable class.
statement_notes.gap: It does not match the available \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) upper bound and does not show that the IPW obstruction raises the minimax risk for every estimator.
statement_notes.consumer: The result supplies the lower endpoint of the common expected-risk bracket.

statement_notes.justification: The retained theorem calibrates the causal blind-fit error and the observable blind-versus-recorded discrepancy against total drift at the actually proved stochastic resolution.
statement_notes.gap: The resolution is \(d_{nm}\).  With fixed complexity and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), \(d_{nm}/b_{nm}\asymp\sqrt n\), so the previous conditional \(b_{nm}\)-scale iff is not advertised.
statement_notes.consumer: HeartSteps-style analyses may use the discrepancy as a coarse warning statistic, with its \(d_{nm}\) resolution stated explicitly.

statement_notes.justification: The exact rank-one calculation is the early kill test and a concrete boundary example for the newly defined blind procedure.
statement_notes.gap: It shows blind failure and diagnostic separation on one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law; it is neither a published-method refutation nor an estimator-independent minimax converse.
statement_notes.consumer: HeartSteps II simulations obtain a fully specified adaptive stress design.

statement_notes.justification: This is conservative secondary support: scalar Freedman bounds and a union bound give direct finite-sample simultaneous coverage.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem does not validate the leave-one-cell-out covariance estimator, positivity of a random studentizer, or asymptotic exactness of a multiplier critical value.
statement_notes.consumer: Predeclared polynomial-size dense query families receive explicit radii with a visible \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) multiplicity cost.

statement_notes.justification: After the matched-rate claim is removed, the live question is first whether the minimax risk follows \(b_{nm}\), \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\), or an intermediate rate; a sharp constant is meaningful only after that exponent gap closes.
statement_notes.gap: Open obligation: construct an observed-data estimator improving the loose upper bound or prove an estimator-independent lower bound larger than \(b_{nm}\), without adding singular-factor predictability or exogeneity.  The current IPW-specific obstruction cannot decide this question.
statement_notes.consumer: A resolution would determine the attainable design-budget and signal-strength law before any sharp-constant calculation.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(t=m/n\).  The aspect-ratio assumption \(\mathrm{ass:aspect\mbox{-}ratio}\) gives \(t\in[c_-,c_+]\).  Choose \(c_0<1\).  On the regime \(b_{nm}\le c_0\), the truncation in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\mbox{-}rate}\) is inactive, and hence, exactly,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 b_{nm}
 &=\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}K r^{3/2}\mu q^{-1/2}
   \sqrt{\log(en)}\sqrt{nm}\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\\
 &=K r^{3/2}\mu\sqrt{t+t^{-1}}
   \frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{n\log(en)}q}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus, with
\[
 s_{nm}:=\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{n\log(en)}q},
\]
there are positive constants \(C_-\) and \(C_+\), depending only on \(r,K,\mu,c_-,c_+\), such that
\[
 C_-s_{nm}\le b_{nm}\le C_+s_{nm}.
 \tag{1}
\]

We construct a constant-propensity subexperiment.  Since \(r\) is fixed, partition \(I\) into disjoint blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_r\), and partition \(J\) into disjoint blocks \(J_1,\ldots,J_r\), with block sizes differing by at most one.  Write \(N_s=|I_s|\) and \(M_s=|J_s|\).  For \(s\ge2\), let \(u_s=N_s^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_{I_s}\), viewed as a vector in \(\mathbb R^n\), and, for every \(s\), let \(v_s=M_s^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_{J_s}\), viewed as a vector in \(\mathbb R^m\).  Let
\[
 u_0=N_1^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_{I_1}.
\]
Fix an anchor \(k_0\in I_1\).  For every \(k\in\mathcal K:=I_1\setminus\{k_0\}\), define
\[
 w_k=\frac{e_k-e_{k_0}}{\sqrt2},\qquad
 \delta=a\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}q},\qquad
 u_k=\frac{u_0+\delta w_k}{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}},
 \tag{2}
\]
where the fixed constant \(a>0\) will be chosen below.  The vectors \(u_0\) and \(w_k\) are orthogonal unit vectors.  Therefore \(u_k\) is a unit vector.  Disjoint block supports then show that
\[
 U_k=(u_k,u_2,\ldots,u_r)\in\mathbb O_{n,r},
 \qquad V=(v_1,\ldots,v_r)\in\mathbb O_{m,r}.
 \]
Also set \(U_0=(u_0,u_2,\ldots,u_r)\), and define
\[
 M_k=\lambda_{nm}U_kV^\top\quad(k\in\mathcal K),
 \qquad M_0=\lambda_{nm}U_0V^\top.
 \tag{3}
\]

We next verify every model restriction used by the construction.  From (1)--(2),
\[
 \delta\sqrt n=a s_{nm}\le aC_-^{-1}b_{nm}le aC_-^{-1}c_0.
 \tag{4}
\]
For a row in \(I_1\), the triangle inequality and (2) give
\[
 \|e_i^\top U_k\|_2
 \le N_1^{-1/2}+\delta/\sqrt2.
 \tag{5}
\]
For a row in \(I_s\), \(s\ge2\), its row norm is \(N_s^{-1/2}\).  Since \(r\) is fixed and the blocks are balanced,
\[
 \max_s\sqrt{n/N_s}\longrightarrow\sqrt r.
\]
The strict inequality \(\mu>1\) supplies positive slack between \(\sqrt r\) and \(\sqrt{\mu r}\).  First choose \(a c_0\) small enough, depending only on that slack and the fixed constants in (4), and then take \(n\) sufficiently large.  Equations (4)--(5) yield
\[
 \|U_k\|_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The same balanced-block calculation, without the perturbation term, gives
\[
 \|V\|_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/m}
 \tag{7}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(m\).  Thus (6) and (7) verify \(\mathrm{ass:left\mbox{-}incoherence}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:right\mbox{-}incoherence}\).  By (3), all \(r\) nonzero singular values of \(M_k\) equal \(\lambda_{nm}\).  Consequently \(\mathrm{ass:exact\mbox{-}rank}\), \(\mathrm{ass:signal\mbox{-}floor}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:condition\mbox{-}number}\) hold, the last because \(1\le K\).

It remains to make the outcomes bounded.  For all sufficiently large dimensions, balanced blocks satisfy \(N_s\ge n/(2r)\) and \(M_s\ge m/(2r)\).  Equations (2)--(3) therefore imply
\[
 \max_{i,j}|(M_k)_{ij}|
 \le \frac{2r\lambda_{nm}}{\sqrt{nm}}
     +aB\sqrt{\frac{2r\log(en)}{qm}}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Choose \(c_1>0\) so that \(2rc_1\le1/4\).  Under \(\lambda_{nm}\le c_1B\sqrt{nm}\), the first term in (8) is at most \(B/4\).  The second is at most \(B/4\) for all sufficiently large \(n,m\), because \(q,r,a\) are fixed and the aspect ratio is bounded.  Hence
\[
 \max_{i,j}|(M_k)_{ij}|\le B/2
 \tag{9}
\]
uniformly over \(k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}\).

For each \(k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}\), define a law \(P_k\) as follows.  Set \(Y_{ij}(0)=0\).  Independently over cells, draw \(Y_{ij}(1)\in\{-B,B\}\) with
\[
 P_k\{Y_{ij}(1)=B\}
 =h_{k,ij}:=\frac12\left(1+\frac{(M_k)_{ij}}B\right).
 \tag{10}
\]
Independently of all potential outcomes and independently over cells, draw \(A_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), and record \(p_{ij}=q\).  Equation (9) puts every \(h_{k,ij}\) in \([1/4,3/4]\), while (10) gives \(E_{P_k}[Y_{ij}(1)]=(M_k)_{ij}\).  Independence from all preceding cells in the row-major filtration of \(\mathrm{def:global\mbox{-}filtration}\) consequently gives
\[
 \mu^1_{ij}=E_{P_k}[Y_{ij}(1)\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]=(M_k)_{ij},
 \qquad \mu^0_{ij}=0.
 \tag{11}
\]
Thus the causal effect matrix \(M=\mu^1-\mu^0\) is exactly \(M_k\), rather than being defined by the observed score.  Independence of \(A_{ij}\) from the potential outcomes, including after conditioning on the recorded past, verifies \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\mbox{-}randomization}\).  Since \(q<1/2\), the equality \(p_{ij}=q\) verifies \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\), and the support in (10), together with \(Y_{ij}(0)=0\), verifies \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\mbox{-}outcomes}\).  Equations (6)--(7), the singular-value calculation following them, and the maintained aspect path verify all remaining member properties of \(\mathrm{def:predictable\mbox{-}class}\).  Hence
\[
 P_k\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)
 \quad\text{for every }k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}.
 \tag{12}
\]
The constant-propensity form is also consistent with the scale calculation in \(\mathrm{prop:fixed\mbox{-}propensity\mbox{-}sanity}\), although (12) has been checked directly.

We now bound the information in the observed experiment \(\mathcal O_{n,m}=\sigma(A,Y,p)\) from \(\mathrm{def:observed\mbox{-}estimators}\).  If \(x,y\in[-B/2,B/2]\), put \(s=(1+x/B)/2\) and \(t'=(1+y/B)/2\).  For fixed \(t'\in[1/4,3/4]\), the Bernoulli relative entropy \(f(s)=s\log(s/t')+(1-s)\log((1-s)/(1-t'))\) satisfies
\[
 f(t')=f'(t')=0,
 \qquad f''(s)=\frac1{s(1-s)}\le\frac{16}3
 \quad\text{on }[1/4,3/4].
\]
Taylor's theorem therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{kl}\left(\frac{1+x/B}{2},\frac{1+y/B}{2}\right)
 \le \frac{2}{3}\frac{(x-y)^2}{B^2}.
 \tag{13}
\]
The assignment law and recorded propensity are identical under \(P_k\) and \(P_0\).  Conditional on \(A_{ij}=0\), the observed outcome is the common value zero; conditional on \(A_{ij}=1\), it has Bernoulli sign parameter \(h_{k,ij}\).  Independence over cells, (13), and the chain rule for the logarithm of the product likelihood thus yield directly
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
 &=q\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{kl}(h_{k,ij},h_{0,ij})\\
 &\le \frac{Cq}{B^2}\|M_k-M_0\|_F^2.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{14}
\]
Only the first singular component differs in (3), and \(\|v_1\|_2=1\), so
\[
 \|M_k-M_0\|_F^2
 =\lambda_{nm}^2\|u_k-u_0\|_2^2.
\]
Moreover, orthogonality in (2) gives
\[
 \|u_k-u_0\|_2^2
 =2\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}}\right)
 \le\delta^2.
\]
Substitution of (2) into (14) proves
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
 \le Ca^2\log(en).
 \tag{15}
\]

The alternatives are separated in the required rowwise loss.  If \(k,\ell\in\mathcal K\) are distinct, inspect row \(k\).  On that row only the first columns of \(U_k\) and \(U_\ell\) can be nonzero, and (2) gives
\[
 \|e_k^\top U_k\|_2-\|e_k^\top U_\ell\|_2
 =\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
\]
Right multiplication by any \(R\in\mathbb O_r\) preserves the first row norm.  The reverse triangle inequality therefore gives
\[
 \min_{R\in\mathbb O_r}\|U_kR-U_\ell\|_{2,\infty}
 \ge\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:rowwise\mbox{-}loss}\),
\[
 \mathcal L(U_k,U_\ell)
 \ge \Delta_{nm}:=sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
       \frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
 \tag{16}
\]
Equation (4) implies \(\delta\to0\), so eventually \(\delta\le1\).  Combining (1), (2), and (16), and using \(t\in[c_-,c_+]\), gives a constant \(c>0\), depending only on the fixed quantities in the theorem, such that
\[
 \Delta_{nm}\ge c b_{nm}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, before the harmless factor in the denominator of (16), the exact ratio is
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\,\delta}{b_{nm}}
 =\frac{a}{K r^2\mu^{3/2}\sqrt{t+t^{-1}}}.
\]

For completeness, we derive the multiple-testing reduction.  Let \(D=|\mathcal K|=N_1-1\), let \(\Theta\) be uniform on \(\mathcal K\), and, conditional on \(\Theta=k\), draw the observed experiment from \(P_k^{\mathcal O}\).  With \(\overline P=D^{-1}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}P_k^{\mathcal O}\), direct expansion of the logarithms gives
\[
 I(\Theta;\mathcal O)
 =\frac1D\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},\overline P)
 =\frac1D\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
  -\operatorname{KL}(\overline P,P_0^{\mathcal O}).
\]
Nonnegativity of relative entropy and (15) imply
\[
 I(\Theta;\mathcal O)\le Ca^2\log(en).
 \tag{18}
\]
For any decoder \(\widehat\Theta\), let \(P_e=P(\widehat\Theta\ne\Theta)\).  Conditioning the entropy of \(\Theta\) first on the error indicator yields
\[
 H(\Theta\mid\mathcal O)\le\log2+P_e\log D.
\]
Since \(H(\Theta)=\log D\), this and (18) give
\[
 P_e\ge1-\frac{Ca^2\log(en)+\log2}{\log D}.
 \tag{19}
\]
Balanced blocks give \(D\asymp n\).  Choose \(a>0\) sufficiently small, depending only on the fixed quantities, so that the right side of (19) is at least \(1/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Finally take any \(\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) and decode by a nearest member of \(\{U_k:k\in\mathcal K\}\) in the orthogonal-quotient \(2,\infty\) distance.  This quotient distance obeys the triangle inequality: composing two optimizing orthogonal alignments and using invariance of row norms under right orthogonal multiplication proves it directly.  Thus, on a decoding error under \(P_k\), pairwise separation (16) and nearest-neighbor decoding imply
\[
 \mathcal L(\widetilde U,U_k)\ge\Delta_{nm}/2.
\]
Averaging over the uniform index, using (19), and then using (17), we obtain
\[
 \sup_{k\in\mathcal K}E_{P_k}[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U_k)]
 \ge\frac{\Delta_{nm}}4
 \ge c_2b_{nm}.
\]
By (12), this finite family is a subset of the frozen predictable class; by construction it has \(p_{ij}=q\) at every cell.  Taking the supremum over the full class and then the infimum over all observed-experiment estimators \(\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) proves the theorem.

Put \(N=nm\), \(d=|\mathcal G_n|\), and fix a deterministic \(g\in\mathcal G_n\).  By \(\mathrm{def:contrast\mbox{-}process}\), the definition of \(\tau_g\), and \(\mathrm{def:ipw\mbox{-}score}\),
\[
 \widehat\tau_g-\tau_g
 =\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}g_{ij}
   \bigl(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}-M_{ij}\bigr)
 =\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}g_{ij}E_{ij}.
\]
For the cell \((i,j)\), write \(\mathcal H_{ij}=\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).  The loading \(g\) is deterministic, and \(\mathrm{lem:ipw\mbox{-}identification}\) gives
\[
 E_P[g_{ij}E_{ij}\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]=0.
\]
Consequently the row-major sequence of summands in the preceding display is a scalar martingale-difference sequence.

We next derive deterministic bounds for its predictable quadratic variation and increments.  Consistency in the definition of \(Y\), followed by iterated conditional expectation and \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\mbox{-}randomization}\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\!\left[(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij})^2\mid\mathcal H_{ij}\right]
 &=E_P\!\left[
   \frac{A_{ij}Y_{ij}(1)^2}{p_{ij}^2}
   +\frac{(1-A_{ij})Y_{ij}(0)^2}{(1-p_{ij})^2}
   \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal H_{ij}\right]\\
 &=E_P\!\left[
   \frac{Y_{ij}(1)^2}{p_{ij}}
   +\frac{Y_{ij}(0)^2}{1-p_{ij}}
   \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal H_{ij}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the denominators are strictly positive by \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\), and each \(p_{ij}\) is \(\mathcal H_{ij}\)-measurable by the definition of the recorded propensity.  Since \(M_{ij}\) is \(\mathcal H_{ij}\)-measurable and \(E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]=M_{ij}\),
\[
 E_P[E_{ij}^2\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]
 =E_P[(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij})^2\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]-M_{ij}^2
 \le \frac{2B^2}{q}.
\]
The last inequality uses \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\mbox{-}outcomes}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\).  The same two assumptions imply
\[
 |Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}|\le \frac{B}{q},
 \qquad
 |M_{ij}|\le
 |E_P[Y_{ij}(1)\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]|
 +|E_P[Y_{ij}(0)\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]|
 \le 2B,
\]
and hence, because \(q<1\),
\[
 |g_{ij}E_{ij}|
 \le \frac{3B}{q}|g_{ij}|
 \le R_g:=\frac{3BC_\infty}{qN},
\]
where the final inequality is \(\mathrm{ass:dense\mbox{-}loadings}\).  Therefore every partial predictable quadratic variation is bounded by its full-sum bound
\[
 \sum_{o(i,j)\le k}E_P[g_{ij}^2E_{ij}^2\mid\mathcal H_{ij}]
 \le \sigma_g^2:=\frac{2B^2}{q}\lVert g\rVert_F^2.
\]
The lower average-loading bound and \(B,q>0\) ensure \(\sigma_g^2>0\), as required for the stated form of Freedman's inequality.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:tropp\mbox{-}matrix\mbox{-}freedman}\) to the \(1\times1\) self-adjoint matrices formed by the partial sums, and apply it again to their negatives.  A union bound over the two signs yields, for every \(t\ge0\),
\[
 P\!\left(\left|\widehat\tau_g-\tau_g\right|\ge t\right)
 \le 2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2}{2(\sigma_g^2+R_gt/3)}\right\}.
\]
For \(x>0\), set
\[
 t_g(x)=\sqrt{2\sigma_g^2x}+\frac{2R_gx}{3}.
\]
Direct expansion gives
\[
 t_g(x)^2-2x\{\sigma_g^2+R_gt_g(x)/3\}
 =\frac{2R_gx}{3}\sqrt{2\sigma_g^2x}\ge0.
\]
Thus the preceding tail bound, together with the displayed values of \(\sigma_g^2\) and \(R_g\), implies
\[
 P\!\left(
 |\widehat\tau_g-\tau_g|>
 2B\sqrt{\frac{\lVert g\rVert_F^2}{q}x}
 +\frac{2BC_\infty}{qN}x
 \right)\le2e^{-x}.
\]

Take \(x=\log(2d/\alpha)>0\), which is valid because \(d\ge2\) by \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial\mbox{-}family}\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  A union bound over the fixed family \(\mathcal G_n\) has failure probability at most
\[
 2d\exp\{-\log(2d/\alpha)\}=\alpha.
\]
On the complementary event, \(|\widehat\tau_g-\tau_g|\le R_{g,\alpha}\) for every \(g\in\mathcal G_n\), which is exactly the asserted simultaneous inclusion.

Finally, \(\mathrm{ass:dense\mbox{-}loadings}\) also gives the uniform bound
\[
 \lVert g\rVert_F^2
 \le N\left(\frac{C_\infty}{N}\right)^2
 =\frac{C_\infty^2}{N}.
\]
Substitution into \(R_{g,\alpha}\), with \(N=nm\), proves uniformly in \(g\) that
\[
 R_{g,\alpha}
 =O\!\left(
 B\sqrt{\frac{\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)}{nmq}}
 +\frac{B\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)}{qnm}
 \right).
\]
The family size enters this direct finite-sample argument only through the union-bound value \(x=\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)\).  In particular, the leading stochastic term has the separate factor \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\), whereas \(b_{nm}\) in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\mbox{-}rate}\) has no dependence on \(\mathcal G_n\).  No step uses \(\widehat s_g\), its positivity or consistency, or the multiplier critical value \(c_{1-\alpha}\); hence the result is a conservative direct-IPW band and does not assert feasible multiplier exactness.

proposed.statement:
Let \(N=nm\) and \(d=|\mathcal G_n|\).  Under the predictable experiment class, polynomial family growth, and deterministic dense average-scale loadings, define
\[
 R_{g,\alpha}=2B\sqrt{\frac{\lVert g\rVert_F^2}{q}\log\!\frac{2d}{\alpha}}
 +\frac{2BC_\infty}{qN}\log\!\frac{2d}{\alpha}.
\]
Then, for every finite \(n,m\),
\[
 P\!\left(\tau_g\in[\widehat\tau_g-R_{g,\alpha},
 \widehat\tau_g+R_{g,\alpha}]\text{ for every }g\in\mathcal G_n\right)
 \ge1-\alpha.
\]
Uniformly in \(g\),
\[
 R_{g,\alpha}=O\!\left(
 B\sqrt{\frac{\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)}{nmq}}
 +\frac{B\log(2|\mathcal G_n|/\alpha)}{qnm}\right).
\]
Thus the simultaneous stochastic radius has the separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) inflation and this factor is not part of \(b_{nm}\).  This conservative finite-sample result makes no claim that the frozen leave-one-cell-out multiplier critical value is asymptotically exact.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The conservative finite-sample proof is a direct scalar-Freedman argument and does not use the oracle high-dimensional multiplier primitives. Removing that obsolete dependency prevents the theorem from inheriting variance-nondegeneracy or suggesting feasible studentizer validity; adding the IPW-score definition declares the score and error identities used directly in the proof.
